failure_summary.description: Agents chose a salient association or partial clue match over the requested relation or category; one also returned source metadata instead of the answer.
Answers missed exact-match granularity in inconsistent directions: one expanded a shared head noun, one shortened a full name, and one supplied a full name where the gold used a surname.

patch.reasoning: The main recurring error is accepting a candidate that matches only part of the clue. A concrete constraint-checking step can address that pattern and help distinguish answer content from metadata. The three answer-form failures require opposite length adjustments, so they do not support a reliable new general rule.

edits.content:
## Check Candidates Against the Whole Clue
Before answering, test a candidate against every defining descriptor and relationship in the clue; matching one salient word or a nearby fact is not enough. When evidence snippets compete, prefer the one that matches the clue's full category and qualifiers, including its timeframe when relevant. Treat page, file, and source headings as metadata rather than answers; if a passage explicitly marks a clue's answer, use that keyed answer.
